pool.text: Martim Afonso de Sousa founded the first Brazilian village of São Vicente.
Jesuit priests founded São Paulo, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.
The settlement of the region's Courtyard of the College began.
Tupinambás launched a series of attacks against the village on 9 July.
Luís Álvares de Castro moved the capital to the village of São Paulo.
The Captaincy of São Paulo and Minas de Ouro was created.
Mário de Andrade published his rhapsodic novel showcasing an abundance of folklore.
São Paulo won its first skyscraper, the Martinelli Building.
São Paulo became the centre of the Constitutionalist Revolution.
Oswald de Andrade published experimental prose highlighting a break with tradition.
The University of São Paulo was founded with the reunion of faculties.
Campo de Marte opened and became the base for a major fleet.
São Paulo gained its first paved highway connecting to the coast.
Teatro de Arena began with students from a newly founded drama art school.
The SPTrans transport system opened to serve the local population.
The city held a large celebration of the Fourth Centenary.
Cantareira State Park was created to protect the water supply.
Iguatemi Faria Lima opened as Brazil's oldest mall.
The Urban Development Plan proposed the Basic Plan for Integrated Development.
The immigrant hostel officially received its very last incoming guests.
